flawed_step: The claim that having the same spectrum means two graphs are isomorphic. The spectrum does not determine a graph up to isomorphism.
counterexample: G1 = the star K_{1,4}: a center joined to 4 leaves, on 5 vertices. G2 = the 4-cycle C_4 plus one isolated vertex, also on 5 vertices. Spectrum of K_{1,4}: in general K_{1,m} has eigenvalues ±sqrt(m) and 0 with multiplicity m-1, so here {2, -2, 0, 0, 0}. Spectrum of C_4: 2cos(2πk/4) for k=0..3 gives {2, 0, -2, 0}. The isolated vertex adds one more 0, so G2 has {2, -2, 0, 0, 0}. The two multisets are equal, so the graphs are cospectral. They are not isomorphic: G1 is connected and has a vertex of degree 4, while G2 is disconnected and every vertex has degree at most 2. Their degree sequences are (4,1,1,1,1) and (2,2,2,2,0).
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The standard counterexample is the star K_{1,4} versus C_4 plus an isolated vertex. Both have 5 vertices and spectrum {2, -2, 0, 0, 0}, but they are not isomorphic because their degree sequences and connectivity differ.
